text: The adjoint representation of a Lie algebra sends $X$ to the operator $\mathrm{ad}(X)$ that acts on $Y$ by $\mathrm{ad}(X)(Y) =$
explanation: By definition $\mathrm{ad}(X)(Y)=[X,Y]$; it is the derivative at the identity of the group conjugation $\mathrm{Ad}$. The map $Y\mapsto XYX^{-1}$ is the group-level $\mathrm{Ad}(g)$ (for a group element), not the algebra $\mathrm{ad}$; plain $XY$ is not bracket-valued; and $[Y,X]=-[X,Y]$ has the wrong sign by antisymmetry.
